scene.label: Act 3, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. Before Lord Hastings' house

content.text: Enter a Messenger to the door of Hastings.

lines.text: My lord, my lord!
lines.plainText: My lord my lord

lines.text: [Within.] Who knocks?
lines.plainText: Within Who knocks

lines.text: One from the Lord Stanley.
lines.plainText: One from the Lord Stanley

lines.text: [Within.] What is't o'clock?
lines.plainText: Within What is't o'clock

lines.text: Upon the stroke of four.
lines.plainText: Upon the stroke of four

lines.text: Cannot my Lord Stanley sleep these tedious nights?
lines.plainText: Cannot my Lord Stanley sleep these tedious nights

lines.text: So it appears by that I have to say.
lines.plainText: So it appears by that I have to say

lines.text: First, he commends him to your noble self.
lines.plainText: First he commends him to your noble self

lines.text: What then?
lines.plainText: What then

lines.text: Then certifies your lordship that this night
lines.plainText: Then certifies your lordship that this night

lines.text: He dreamt the boar had razed off his helm.
lines.plainText: He dreamt the boar had razed off his helm

lines.text: Besides, he says there are two councils kept,
lines.plainText: Besides he says there are two councils kept

lines.text: And that may be determined at the one
lines.plainText: And that may be determined at the one

lines.text: Which may make you and him to rue at th' other.
lines.plainText: Which may make you and him to rue at th' other

lines.text: Therefore he sends to know your lordship's pleasure,
lines.plainText: Therefore he sends to know your lordship's pleasure

lines.text: If you will presently take horse with him
lines.plainText: If you will presently take horse with him

lines.text: And with all speed post with him toward the north,
lines.plainText: And with all speed post with him toward the north

lines.text: To shun the danger that his soul divines.
lines.plainText: To shun the danger that his soul divines

lines.text: Go, fellow, go. Return unto thy lord;
lines.plainText: Go fellow go Return unto thy lord

lines.text: Bid him not fear the separated council.
lines.plainText: Bid him not fear the separated council

lines.text: His honour and myself are at the one,
lines.plainText: His honour and myself are at the one

lines.text: And at the other is my good friend Catesby,
lines.plainText: And at the other is my good friend Catesby

lines.text: Where nothing can proceed that toucheth us
lines.plainText: Where nothing can proceed that toucheth us

lines.text: Whereof I shall not have intelligence.
lines.plainText: Whereof I shall not have intelligence

lines.text: Tell him his fears are shallow, without instance.
lines.plainText: Tell him his fears are shallow without instance

lines.text: And for his dreams, I wonder he's so simple
lines.plainText: And for his dreams I wonder he's so simple

lines.text: To trust the mockery of unquiet slumbers.
lines.plainText: To trust the mockery of unquiet slumbers

lines.text: To fly the boar before the boar pursues
lines.plainText: To fly the boar before the boar pursues

lines.text: Were to incense the boar to follow us,
lines.plainText: Were to incense the boar to follow us

lines.text: And make pursuit where he did mean no chase.
lines.plainText: And make pursuit where he did mean no chase

lines.text: Go, bid thy master rise and come to me,
lines.plainText: Go bid thy master rise and come to me

lines.text: And we will both together to the Tower,
lines.plainText: And we will both together to the Tower

lines.text: Where he shall see the boar will use us kindly.
lines.plainText: Where he shall see the boar will use us kindly

lines.text: I'll go, my lord, and tell him what you say.
lines.plainText: I'll go my lord and tell him what you say

lines.text: Many good morrows to my noble lord.
lines.plainText: Many good morrows to my noble lord

lines.text: Good morrow, Catesby; you are early stirring.
lines.plainText: Good morrow Catesby you are early stirring

lines.text: What news, what news in this our tott'ring state?
lines.plainText: What news what news in this our tott'ring state

lines.text: It is a reeling world indeed, my lord,
lines.plainText: It is a reeling world indeed my lord

lines.text: And I believe will never stand upright
lines.plainText: And I believe will never stand upright

lines.text: Till Richard wear the garland of the realm.
lines.plainText: Till Richard wear the garland of the realm

lines.text: How, wear the garland? Dost thou mean the crown?
lines.plainText: How wear the garland Dost thou mean the crown

lines.text: Ay, my good lord.
lines.plainText: Ay my good lord

lines.text: I'll have this crown of mine cut from my shoulders
lines.plainText: I'll have this crown of mine cut from my shoulders

lines.text: Before I'll see the crown so foul misplaced.
lines.plainText: Before I'll see the crown so foul misplaced

lines.text: But canst thou guess that he doth aim at it?
lines.plainText: But canst thou guess that he doth aim at it

lines.text: Ay, on my life, and hopes to find you forward
lines.plainText: Ay on my life and hopes to find you forward

lines.text: Upon his party for the gain thereof;
lines.plainText: Upon his party for the gain thereof

lines.text: And thereupon he sends you this good news,
lines.plainText: And thereupon he sends you this good news

lines.text: That this same very day your enemies,
lines.plainText: That this same very day your enemies

lines.text: The kindred of the Queen, must die at Pomfret.
lines.plainText: The kindred of the Queen must die at Pomfret

lines.text: Indeed, I am no mourner for that news,
lines.plainText: Indeed I am no mourner for that news

lines.text: Because they have been still my adversaries.
lines.plainText: Because they have been still my adversaries

lines.text: But that I'll give my voice on Richard's side
lines.plainText: But that I'll give my voice on Richard's side

lines.text: To bar my master's heirs in true descent,
lines.plainText: To bar my master's heirs in true descent

lines.text: God knows I will not do it, to the death.
lines.plainText: God knows I will not do it to the death

lines.text: God keep your lordship in that gracious mind.
lines.plainText: God keep your lordship in that gracious mind

lines.text: But I shall laugh at this a twelve-month hence,
lines.plainText: But I shall laugh at this a twelvemonth hence

lines.text: That they which brought me in my master's hate,
lines.plainText: That they which brought me in my master's hate

lines.text: I live to look upon their tragedy.
lines.plainText: I live to look upon their tragedy

lines.text: Well, Catesby, ere a fortnight make me older
lines.plainText: Well Catesby ere a fortnight make me older

lines.text: I'll send some packing that yet think not on't.
lines.plainText: I'll send some packing that yet think not on't

lines.text: 'Tis a vile thing to die, my gracious lord,
lines.plainText: 'Tis a vile thing to die my gracious lord

lines.text: When men are unprepared and look not for it.
lines.plainText: When men are unprepared and look not for it

lines.text: O monstrous, monstrous! And so falls it out
lines.plainText: O monstrous monstrous And so falls it out

lines.text: With Rivers, Vaughan, Grey; and so 'twill do
lines.plainText: With Rivers Vaughan Grey and so 'twill do

lines.text: With some men else that think themselves as safe
lines.plainText: With some men else that think themselves as safe

lines.text: As thou and I, who, as thou know'st, are dear
lines.plainText: As thou and I who as thou know'st are dear

lines.text: To princely Richard and to Buckingham.
lines.plainText: To princely Richard and to Buckingham

lines.text: The Princes both make high account of you—
lines.plainText: The Princes both make high account of you

lines.text: [Aside.] For they account his head upon the Bridge.
lines.plainText: Aside For they account his head upon the Bridge

lines.text: I know they do, and I have well deserved it.
lines.plainText: I know they do and I have well deserved it

lines.text: My lord, good morrow; good morrow, Catesby.
lines.plainText: My lord good morrow good morrow Catesby

lines.text: You may jest on, but, by the Holy Rood,
lines.plainText: You may jest on but by the Holy Rood

lines.text: I do not like these several councils, I.
lines.plainText: I do not like these several councils I

lines.text: My lord, I hold my life as dear as you do yours,
lines.plainText: My lord I hold my life as dear as you do yours

lines.text: And never in my days, I do protest,
lines.plainText: And never in my days I do protest

lines.text: Was it so precious to me as 'tis now.
lines.plainText: Was it so precious to me as 'tis now

lines.text: Think you, but that I know our state secure,
lines.plainText: Think you but that I know our state secure

lines.text: I would be so triumphant as I am?
lines.plainText: I would be so triumphant as I am

lines.text: The lords at Pomfret, when they rode from London,
lines.plainText: The lords at Pomfret when they rode from London

lines.text: Were jocund and supposed their states were sure,
lines.plainText: Were jocund and supposed their states were sure

lines.text: And they indeed had no cause to mistrust;
lines.plainText: And they indeed had no cause to mistrust

lines.text: But yet you see how soon the day o'ercast.
lines.plainText: But yet you see how soon the day o'ercast

lines.text: This sudden stab of rancour I misdoubt;
lines.plainText: This sudden stab of rancour I misdoubt

lines.text: Pray God, I say, I prove a needless coward.
lines.plainText: Pray God I say I prove a needless coward

lines.text: What, shall we toward the Tower? The day is spent.
lines.plainText: What shall we toward the Tower The day is spent

lines.text: Come, come. Have with you. Wot you what, my lord?
lines.plainText: Come come Have with you Wot you what my lord

lines.text: Today the lords you talked of are beheaded.
lines.plainText: Today the lords you talked of are beheaded

lines.text: They, for their truth, might better wear their heads
lines.plainText: They for their truth might better wear their heads

lines.text: Than some that have accused them wear their hats.
lines.plainText: Than some that have accused them wear their hats

lines.text: But come, my lord, let's away.
lines.plainText: But come my lord let's away

lines.text: Go on before; I'll talk with this good fellow.
lines.plainText: Go on before I'll talk with this good fellow

lines.text: The better that your lordship please to ask.
lines.plainText: The better that your lordship please to ask

lines.text: I tell thee, man, 'tis better with me now
lines.plainText: I tell thee man 'tis better with me now

lines.text: Than when thou met'st me last where now we meet.
lines.plainText: Than when thou met'st me last where now we meet

lines.text: Then was I going prisoner to the Tower,
lines.plainText: Then was I going prisoner to the Tower

lines.text: By the suggestion of the Queen's allies.
lines.plainText: By the suggestion of the Queen's allies

lines.text: But now, I tell thee—keep it to thyself—
lines.plainText: But now I tell theekeep it to thyself

lines.text: This day those enemies are put to death,
lines.plainText: This day those enemies are put to death

lines.text: And I in better state than e'er I was.
lines.plainText: And I in better state than e'er I was

lines.text: God hold it, to your honour's good content!
lines.plainText: God hold it to your honour's good content

lines.text: Gramercy, fellow. There, drink that for me.
lines.plainText: Gramercy fellow There drink that for me

lines.text: I thank your honour.
lines.plainText: I thank your honour

lines.text: Well met, my lord; I am glad to see your honour.
lines.plainText: Well met my lord I am glad to see your honour

lines.text: I thank thee, good Sir John, with all my heart.
lines.plainText: I thank thee good Sir John with all my heart

lines.text: I am in your debt for your last exercise.
lines.plainText: I am in your debt for your last exercise

lines.text: Come the next sabbath, and I will content you.
lines.plainText: Come the next sabbath and I will content you

lines.text: I'll wait upon your lordship.
lines.plainText: I'll wait upon your lordship

lines.text: What, talking with a priest, Lord Chamberlain?
lines.plainText: What talking with a priest Lord Chamberlain

lines.text: Your friends at Pomfret, they do need the priest;
lines.plainText: Your friends at Pomfret they do need the priest

lines.text: Your honour hath no shriving work in hand.
lines.plainText: Your honour hath no shriving work in hand

lines.text: Good faith, and when I met this holy man,
lines.plainText: Good faith and when I met this holy man

lines.text: The men you talk of came into my mind.
lines.plainText: The men you talk of came into my mind

lines.text: What, go you toward the Tower?
lines.plainText: What go you toward the Tower

lines.text: I do, my lord, but long I cannot stay there.
lines.plainText: I do my lord but long I cannot stay there

lines.text: I shall return before your lordship thence.
lines.plainText: I shall return before your lordship thence

lines.text: Nay, like enough, for I stay dinner there.
lines.plainText: Nay like enough for I stay dinner there

lines.text: [Aside.] And supper too, although thou knowest it not.
lines.plainText: Aside And supper too although thou knowest it not

lines.text: Come, will you go?
lines.plainText: Come will you go

lines.text: I'll wait upon your lordship.
lines.plainText: I'll wait upon your lordship
